conventions.convention: The circle is multiplicative, with angular coordinates modulo 2π; the character at angle λ is h ↦ exp(ihλ). The integer group is discrete and its dual carries the compact-open topology.
Angular Lebesgue measure is the Borel pushforward from [-π,π), has mass 2π, and assumes Countable Choice. It is not defined here as a completed circle measure.
For a real weakly stationary process, γ(h)=Cov(X_(t+h),X_t), and the spectral representation uses γ(h)=∫exp(ihλ)F(dλ). A density is relative to unnormalized angular measure.
The periodogram uses observations t=1,…,n, n≥1, population-mean centering, negative exponential phase, and normalization 1/(2πn). The Fejér kernel has the same normalization.
Smoothing uses a nonnegative continuous compactly supported kernel of integral one with K(0)>0, its periodization, and normalized weights on λ_(j,n)=2πj/n for 0≤j<n.

Spectral-measure existence assumes AC and DC. Finite expectation and convolution with a supplied spectral measure need no choice principle; angular-density and smoothing conclusions assume Countable Choice.
The sinusoid has v>0 and frequency strictly between 0 and π; the AR(1) branch permits σ²=0 and ρ=0, with |ρ|<1 and ρ⁰=1.

load_bearing.statement: A spectral measure is a finite positive Radon Borel measure F on the circle satisfying γ(h)=∫exp(ihλ)F(dλ) for every integer h. The known-mean periodogram is I_n(λ)=(2πn)^(-1)|Σ_(t=1)^n(X_t−μ)exp(−itλ)|².
Assume Countable Choice. For every integer k, with unnormalized angular Lebesgue measure, ∫exp(ikλ)dλ equals 2π when k=0 and zero otherwise.
For discrete Z and the multiplicative unit circle, Ψ(z)(n)=zⁿ is a group isomorphism and a homeomorphism onto the Pontryagin dual with its compact-open topology.

Assume AC and DC. Every real weakly stationary process has a unique finite positive Radon spectral measure F, with mass γ(0). If Σ_h|γ(h)|<∞, then F has continuous nonnegative density f(λ)=(2π)^(-1)Σ_hγ(h)exp(−ihλ).

For every n≥1, E[I_n(λ)]=(2π)^(-1)Σ_(|h|<n)(1−|h|/n)γ(h)exp(−ihλ), equivalently ∫Φ_n(λ−θ)F(dθ) for a supplied spectral measure. Under Countable Choice, an integrable spectral density continuous at λ₀, the defined kernel, b_n→0 and nb_n→∞, the smoothing weights eventually exist and E[ṽf_n(λ₀)]→f(λ₀).

concerns.concern: Proof 3.1, source line 125, contains four doubled-backslash setminus commands, for example the literal source text U\\setminus E. These should be ordinary set-difference commands; the doubled backslash introduces a TeX row-break command instead. The surrounding regularity argument is mathematically sound.

alerts.finding: In thm-stationary-arma-spectral-density, Proof 4.1 says “the middle integral is 1 when h-j+k=0 and 0 otherwise,” using normalized angular Fourier orthogonality. The local supplier lem-angular-fourier-orthogonality proves exactly this identity under Countable Choice, which the consumer assumes, but it is absent from the consumer's deps and Facts, and from its batch-42 cross-batch dependency input. The cited F5 supplies Tonelli for coefficient sums, not this integral evaluation. Record the implicit supplier edge and cite it, or supply the elementary integral derivation.

seams_checked.note: The opened stationarity and autocovariance definitions supply precisely real integer-indexed coordinates, finite second moments, constant mean, and γ(h)=Cov(X_(t+h),X_t). No strict-stationarity, ergodic or CLT conclusion is imported.

The ARMA spectral theorem preserves the positive-phase covariance representation, angular mass 2π, density normalization and Countable Choice premise. It constructs its density directly rather than assuming the AC+DC Herglotz existence conclusion. Its undeclared orthogonality use is separately alerted.

This is contextual rather than a direct item dependency. The spatial Bochner theorem uses the Pontryagin dual of R^d under AC+DC and asserts a measure representation without a density. It does not transfer the discrete-Z circle identification or periodogram normalization to spatial fields.
